answer: Sybil resistance works best as a bonded jetty rule: before a new identity may attest to anyone, it must stake a deposit, and its votes count only when a separate, older identity vouches that it is not run by the same operator. The ledger keeps a mirror hash of each account's funding source and writing rhythm, so a thousand sock puppets fed by one wallet collapse into a single cluster and lose their shared basalt stake in one slash. Faking identities then costs more than the rewards they can farm, which is the whole point.
